FXUS62 KMFL 181120
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
620 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 617 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

  - There is an increased threat of urban flooding along the east
    coast of South Florida the next few days. Impactful flash
    flooding is ongoing across portions of SE Florida and this 
    risk is expected to continue over the coming days.
 
  - Flood Watch in effect for all of Southeast Florida through 
    Thursday evening.

  - Dangerous marine conditions continue across local waters with
    sustained winds between 20-30 kts with isolated gusts to 35
    kts. Atlantic seas are expected to climb to 8-12 feet through
    Thursday, with 4-6 feet across Gulf waters.
 
  - Life threatening rip currents and dangerous surf are forecast
    for Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach beaches through the
    remainder of this week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Thursday)
Issued at 1232 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

Heavy rainfall remains the main concern through the short term 
period as a complex and somewhat uncertain weather pattern continues 
to play out. At the surface, high pressure remains entrenched across 
the eastern seaboard north of Florida, while a weak area of low 
pressure continues to meander across the Gulf. Higher up in the 
atmosphere, a shortwave continues to slowly progress eastward across 
the Gulf coast states which could aid to maintain the surface low, 
or even lead to a gradual strengthening over the next couple of 
days. A stationary boundary associated with this system remains 
draped across the Florida peninsula today and likely tomorrow as 
well which will act to maintain a quite impressive plume of moisture 
across the Southern Florida peninsula. PWATs from the 00Z MFL 
sounding were 1.74 inches which sits just at about the 90th 
percentile for this time of year, although modeled PWATs rise into 
the 1.8-2.0" range over the coming 24 hours, which would be 
extremely impressive for November. In the past 24 hours, portions of 
coastal SE Florida have received between 3-5" with coastal Broward 
and NE Miami-Dade receiving the highest totals. While we are 
currently in a lull during the late overnight hours tonight, the 
stage remains set for additional heavy rainfall today and Thursday, 
with coastal convergence being the primary concern which could lead 
to training cells and flash flooding across urban areas. 

Global models still remain a bit confused on the evolution of this 
surface low, and latest GFS/EURO runs show an additional surface low 
deepening  across the western Atlantic late on Thursday. The exact 
progression of this feature will determine where the stationary 
boundary meanders over the coming days, which will determine exactly 
where the highest rainfall totals will fall. Despite this, I can 
speak broadly that the eastern coastal areas of South Florida will 
continue to be favored today and tomorrow for periods of heavy 
rainfall. Rainfall totals over the next 48 hours will broadly be in 
the 2-4" range across most areas of SE Florida, although a 
reasonable worst case could bring an additional 5-8" especially for 
areas that receive repeated rounds of rainfall. A Flood Watch 
remains in effect through Thursday evening. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Thursday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 1232 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

On Friday, global models depict multiple areas of low pressure 
across the Gulf and western Atlantic. Our original area of low 
pressure remains in the Gulf while an additional lobe of 
vorticity is able to break off into the western Atlantic and 
becomes the dominant feature. Across the eastern CONUS, high 
pressure at the surface begins to breakdown as a cold front sweeps
across the central United States. Before the arrival of drier air for
the weekend, perhaps one additional day of heavy rainfall
potential on Friday, especially earlier in the day as PWATs remain
maximized and will still approach 2". Exact forecast for Friday
will be heavily dependent on the evolution of the surface lows,
however, so I would place confidence on this portion of the
forecast on the lower end for now. The cold front sweeping across
the central CONUS and retreat of high pressure will help pull the
low over the western Atlantic towards the north and finally usher
in drier air across the area through the weekend timeframe. As 
this system deepens and races off to the north, PWATs drop into 
the 1.2-1.3" range and Saturday and continue to fall to perhaps 
below 1" on Sunday and Monday. This should help limit rain chances
through the weekend, although there will still be a chance 
(10-20%) for scattered shower activity each day through the 
weekend and early next week. 

Moisture begins to return heading towards the middle portion of the 
week as an area of low pressure slides across the Gulf states. This 
will likely be our next shot for more significant rainfall although 
details will become clearer over the coming days. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 617 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

Periods of sub-VFR conditions will be likely through the period as
repeated bands of SHRA/TSRA move across the area. Timing remains
uncertain, but TEMPOs and PROB30 groups are in place for all 
sites between 16-20Z, and later on from 00-06Z. Winds will remain
brisk, with sustained winds up to 20 kts and gusts up to 30 kts 
through the day. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1232 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

Strong northeasterly winds will result in hazardous conditions 
across all local waters of South Florida through the next couple 
of days. Easterly winds between 25-30 kts will be likely through 
the day with isolated gusts to 35 kts possible. 8-12 foot seas are
possible across Atlantic waters over the next couple of days with
4-6 feet across Gulf waters. Small Craft Advisories are in effect
through Thursday night.

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 1232 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

High risk of rip currents across SE Florida beaches as gusty
onshore flow continues. A High Surf Advisory is in effect for 
Palm Beach County beaches and Broward County beaches as surf 
height could reach 7-10 feet through Thursday. 

&&

data.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 11:08AM EST until November 18 at 12:45PM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northern Miami-Dade County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1245 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1107 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor to moderate
flooding. An upgrade to a Flash Flood Warning could be needed.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Miami, Hialeah, Coral Gables, South Miami, Kendall, Doral,
Pinecrest, Miami Springs, Miami Shores, West Miami, El Portal,
Medley, Miami International Airport, Coral Terrace, Coconut
Grove, University Of Miami, Marlins Park, Westchester, Glenvar
Heights and Downtown Miami.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
data.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

data.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Biscayne Bay...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...

* Until noon EST.

* At 1054 AM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located over Biscayne Bay, moving northwest at 20
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

Virginia Key, Convoy Point, Turkey Point, Card Sound, Key Biscayne,
Biscayne Bay, North Bay Village, Indian Creek, Bay Harbor Islands,
Miami Beach, and Coral Gables.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

data.headline: Flood Watch issued November 18 at 2:21AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Far South Miami-Dade County, Inland Broward
County, Inland Miami-Dade County, Inland Palm Beach County, Metro
Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami
Dade.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of storms may produce rainfall amounts of 2 to 4
inches through late Thursday. Higher amounts of 6 to 8 inches
with locally isolated amounts over 10 inches may be possible.
Heavy rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour may observed with
some of these storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
data.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

data.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 2:20AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

data.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
700 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

A non-tropical low pressure system is expected to form near the 
northern Bahamas by this weekend.  This system has some potential 
for subtropical development while it moves northward or 
northeastward near or offshore of the southeastern  U.S. coast 
through the weekend.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.
